headline: Advance Reservations for Slot Canyons and Marina Slips
reservation: Access to Upper and Lower Antelope Canyon is restricted to guided tours by Navajo operators; reservations often fill months ahead. Lake Powell boat rentals and slip spaces at Antelope Point Marina require separate advanced booking. Always verify the latest Navajo Nation and Glen Canyon National Recreation Area entry requirements via official sites as systems change.

days.title: Canyon Depths and Colorado Curves

stops.name: Antelope Canyon
stops.detail: Join a pre-booked Navajo-led tour to walk through sculpted sandstone walls and witness light beams in the upper or lower chambers.

stops.name: Horseshoe Bend
stops.detail: Walk the accessible trail to the cliff edge where the Colorado River completes a 270-degree turn 1,000 feet below.

days.driving: Allow 30-60 minutes; conditions vary by seasonal traffic
days.note: Book slot canyon tours at least 3-6 months in advance for peak months.

days.title: Lake Powell and Engineering Feats
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Lake Powell Boulevard

stops.name: Glen Canyon Dam
stops.detail: Visit the Carl Hayden Visitor Center to learn about the dam's construction and its role in regional water management.

stops.name: Wahweap Marina
stops.detail: Access the water for kayaking or a narrated boat tour to view the vast sandstone shoreline from the reservoir.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; local transfers depend on boat launch queues
days.note: Check water levels and boat ramp status at the Glen Canyon official site before arrival.

days.title: High Desert Hikes and History

stops.name: Hanging Garden Trail
stops.detail: A short trek leading to a hidden lush seep of ferns growing directly from the sandstone walls.

stops.name: The Beehives
stops.detail: Scramble over unique sandstone mounds that feature distinct horizontal erosion layers resembling old-fashioned hives.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; desert roads are subject to flash flood closures
days.note: Avoid hiking during midday in summer when temperatures frequently exceed 100 degrees.

intel.title: Tribal Land Access
intel.text: Much of the land surrounding Page is Navajo Nation territory; specific permits or guides are required for off-road areas. Respect all posted signage and stay on designated paths.

intel.title: Regional Gateway Supply
intel.text: Page serves as the primary fuel and grocery hub between Flagstaff and Kanab. Refill tanks here before venturing toward the North Rim or remote Grand Staircase areas.

intel.title: Monsoon Awareness
intel.text: Afternoon thunderstorms in July and August can cause sudden flash floods in slot canyons even without local rain. Always prioritize guide instructions and weather alerts during these months.

intel.title: Desert Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is reliable in Page town center but drops quickly when entering the deep canyons or lake areas. Download offline maps for navigation near Marble Canyon.

intel.title: Horseshoe Bend Staging
intel.text: The dedicated parking area requires a fee and can reach capacity during sunset. Arrive early or utilize local shuttle options if available during peak holidays.

plan.arrival: Collect a rental vehicle at Page Municipal Airport (PGA); stock up on water and high-SPF sunscreen at the supermarkets along Lake Powell Blvd before hotel check-in.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is sufficient for town and main sites, but high-clearance vehicles are recommended for those exploring unpaved backroads. Check rental contracts for off-road exclusions.
plan.goldenHour: Horseshoe Bend Overlook; winter light provides softer hues while summer sunsets are often vibrant due to monsoon dust.
